quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Dad packing his briefcase before heading to work"?
quests.hint: Think about when grown-ups usually leave the house to go to their jobs.
quests.explanation: Yes! Most people head off to work in the morning, as the day begins.
quests.funFact: The word 'briefcase' comes from carrying important papers, called 'briefs'!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A family gathered around watching a movie at home"?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually relax together after a long day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Family movie time is often a cozy evening activity.
quests.funFact: The very first movies ever made had no sound or color at all!

quests.instruction: "Watching cartoons before getting ready for school" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the busy morning routine before heading out the door to class.
quests.explanation: Yes! Many children watch a little television in the morning before school starts.
quests.funFact: Some of the very first cartoons were made over 100 years ago!

quests.instruction: "Locking the front door before everyone goes to sleep" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the safety habit families do right before heading to bed.
quests.explanation: Yes! Locking up the house is a safety habit done before everyone sleeps.
quests.funFact: Locks have been used to keep homes safe for thousands of years!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Climbing the monkey bars at the playground"?
quests.hint: Think about when children usually visit the playground to play.
quests.explanation: Yes! Playgrounds are full of climbing and playing while it's light outside.
quests.funFact: Monkey bars help children build strong arms and good grip!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A security guard walking his rounds with a flashlight". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when a flashlight is actually needed to see clearly.
quests.explanation: Yes! Flashlights are needed when it's dark, so this happens after the sun sets.
quests.funFact: Security guards help keep buildings and neighborhoods safe while most people sleep!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Grandma reading the newspaper on the porch". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when the newspaper is fresh and delivered for the day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Newspapers are usually read in the morning, once they've been delivered.
quests.funFact: Newspapers have been printed and delivered to homes for over 300 years!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The last dish being dried and put away after supper"?
quests.hint: Think about the chore families finish up before settling in for the evening.
quests.explanation: Yes! Finishing up the dishes after the evening meal happens as the day winds down.
quests.funFact: Dish towels have been used to dry dishes for hundreds of years!

quests.instruction: "Colorful umbrellas lined up at a busy street fair" — is this something we usually see in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when street fairs are usually busiest, with families walking around.
quests.explanation: Yes! Street fairs are lively outdoor events, most crowded during the day.
quests.funFact: Umbrellas were first used for shade from the sun, long before they were used for rain!

quests.instruction: "A cat's eyes glowing in a dark room" — is this something we usually see in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when a room needs to be dark for eyes to glow like that.
quests.explanation: Yes! A cat's eyes glow like this in a dark room, once it's gotten late.
quests.funFact: A cat's eyes have a special layer that helps them see well in dim light!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Riding in a car with the windows rolled down"?
quests.hint: Think about when it feels nice to let the warm breeze in through the window.
quests.explanation: Yes! People often roll down their windows on a warm, sunny drive.
quests.funFact: The first cars didn't even have windows that could roll up or down!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Foxes creeping quietly through the forest"?
quests.hint: Think about when foxes usually come out to search for food.
quests.explanation: Yes! Foxes are mostly active after dark, quietly hunting for food.
quests.funFact: A fox's excellent hearing can pick up the tiniest rustling sounds in the grass!

quests.instruction: "A lemonade stand set up on the corner" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when kids set up a stand to sell cold drinks on a hot day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Lemonade stands pop up on warm, sunny days when people are out walking.
quests.funFact: Lemonade stands are a classic way kids learn about running a small business!

quests.instruction: "A campfire crackling under a starry sky" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when campers gather around a fire to stay warm.
quests.explanation: Yes! Campfires are lit in the evening, once stars begin to appear.
quests.funFact: Sitting around a fire together has been a favorite tradition for thousands of years!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Squirrels scurrying up and down a tree trunk". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when squirrels are usually busy gathering nuts and acorns.
quests.explanation: Yes! Squirrels are active during the day, scurrying around collecting food.
quests.funFact: A squirrel can remember the location of thousands of buried nuts!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Checking that all the windows are shut tight before bed". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about the safety check families do right before heading to sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Checking the windows is one more thing families do right before bed.
quests.funFact: Closed windows also help keep a bedroom warm and cozy through a chilly night!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A garden full of tall, blooming sunflowers"?
quests.hint: Think about the flower that turns its face to follow the sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sunflowers open up and face the sun while it's out.
quests.funFact: Young sunflowers actually turn to track the sun as it moves across the sky!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A baby being rocked gently to sleep"?
quests.hint: Think about the gentle routine parents use to help a baby drift off.
quests.explanation: Yes! Rocking a baby to sleep is a calming bedtime routine.
quests.funFact: The gentle back-and-forth motion of rocking can help babies feel calm and safe!

quests.instruction: "Feeding hay to the horses in the barn" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when farmers usually do most of their animal chores.
quests.explanation: Yes! Farmers usually feed and care for animals during daylight hours.
quests.funFact: A horse can eat almost 20 pounds of hay in just one day!

quests.instruction: "The porch light flickering on automatically as it gets dark" — is this something we usually see in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what a porch light is actually meant to help us see.
quests.explanation: Yes! Porch lights turn on to help light the way once it gets dark outside.
quests.funFact: Some porch lights use a sensor that switches them on all by themselves!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A splash pad spraying cool water for kids"?
quests.hint: Think about when it feels good to cool off from the warm sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! Splash pads are a fun way to cool off on a warm, sunny day.
quests.funFact: Splash pads use much less water than a full swimming pool!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A ferry boat gliding across dark water, lights twinkling"?
quests.hint: Think about when the water would look dark, with only twinkling lights to see by.
quests.explanation: Yes! The water looks dark like this once the sun has fully set.
quests.funFact: Boats use special lights so other ships can spot them safely in the dark!

quests.instruction: "Watching a puppet show at the park" — is this something we usually see in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when families gather outside at the park for shows and events.
quests.explanation: Yes! Puppet shows at the park are usually held during the day.
quests.funFact: Puppet shows have entertained children and families for thousands of years!

quests.instruction: "Setting out a glass of water beside the bed" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the small habit some people do right before turning in for sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Setting out a glass of water is a small habit done just before bed.
quests.funFact: Staying hydrated overnight can help you feel refreshed in the morning!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A construction crew building a new house". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when workers need bright light to safely build something.
quests.explanation: Yes! Construction work is usually done during the day, when it's easy to see.
quests.funFact: Building a whole house can take construction crews several months to finish!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A hedgehog rustling through fallen leaves in the dark". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about the small, spiky animal that comes out once it's dark to search for bugs.
quests.explanation: Yes! Hedgehogs are nocturnal, meaning they're awake and searching for food after dark.
quests.funFact: A hedgehog can curl itself into a tight, spiky little ball to stay safe!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Carrying grocery bags in from the car"?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually go out to shop for food.
quests.explanation: Yes! Grocery shopping is a common daytime errand for families.
quests.funFact: The very first grocery carts were invented so shoppers didn't have to carry heavy baskets!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The very last light in the house switching off"?
quests.hint: Think about the final light turned off before the whole house settles in to sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! The last light switches off once everyone is ready for sleep.
quests.funFact: A completely dark room can help your body know it's finally time to rest!

quests.instruction: "An ice cream truck playing its cheerful song" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when it's hot enough outside to want a cold treat.
quests.explanation: Yes! Ice cream trucks usually drive around during the warm daylight hours.
quests.funFact: Ice cream trucks play music so people can hear them coming from far away!

quests.instruction: "A grandfather clock chiming late in the evening" — is this something we usually see in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what 'late in the evening' means — is it early or very late in the day?
quests.explanation: Yes! Late evening happens well after the sun has gone down.
quests.funFact: Grandfather clocks are named for their tall, standing shape, like a grandfather!
